question: On 2 June 2022 an Italian citizen, Maurizio Cocco, was remanded in custody and transferred to Abidjan prison, a facility where sanitary conditions are appalling1, in part because it holds 12 000 inmates when it only has capacity for 1 500.

Mr Cocco was initially accused of being part of an international drug trafficking and money laundering conspiracy but, following an investigation, he was acquitted by the Economic and Financial Crimes Tribunal in Cocody. However, because of accusations of tax fraud, Mr Cocco is still being unlawfully detained, even though the competent authority has never formally charged him2.

Given that the conditions in which Mr Cocco is being held are deplorable constitute a violation of his human rights, and in the light of the provisions of Article 20 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union and of the EU’s ongoing cooperation agreements – including the 2016 Economic Partnership Agreement – with Côte d’Ivoire: 1.
Will the Vice-President / High Representative turn to the EU Delegation in Abidjan and/or employ other means to assist Italy’s consular authorities to shed light on Mr Cocco’s case?
What diplomatic action will he take to uphold the civil rights of Mr Cocco, an EU citizen?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.4.2024) The EU Delegation in Côte d’Ivoire, despite not having consular competency, is aware of this case and is in close contact with the Italian Embassy present in the country. The Italian Ambassador and Italian consular services are actively following this case.

More generally, it is to be noted that the EU has been funding several projects regarding penal reform as well as detention conditions, with the specific objectives of reducing over-population in various prisons across the country, improving prisoners’ conditions, as well as reducing the pre-trial detention rate.

A new programme (Project RADARS ‘Renforcer Activement les droits des détenus, Améliorer leur Réinsertion sociale et leur Santé’)1 started recently, aimed at improving the health conditions of prisoners and offering opportunities for professional reinsertion. The EU Delegation to Côte d’Ivoire has a regular political and policy dialogue regarding the respect of human rights and law enforcement institutions.
